task_title: docs(CF-176) final: shipped prose reports the disabled row; transcript scoped; sibling artifact corrected
task_criteria: At commit e0ff859: docs/SCHEDULER-ADMISSION.md contains no claim that the code-factory family is fully enabled (grep for the removed assertion returns 0 matches), states the measured 17 ceiling-bearing rows / 16 enabled with code-factory-qa enabled=0 via auto-disable, and carries exactly one sqlite query printing each ratio beside its enabled flag. docs/audits/code-factory-docs-2026-11-04-cf169-validator-claim.md no longer states all rows are enabled=1 and attributes the correction to CF-176. docs/audits/code-factory-docs-2026-11-04-CF-176.md quotes literal outputs for both queries, explains why the audit itself retains the removed phrase, records SELFTEST: PASS at the base and both implementation commits, and RESULT: OK from scripts/boardctl validate.

(5) docs/audits/code-factory-docs-2026-11-04-CF-176.md §3 quotes literal outputs for both queries: grep -n before (lines 54-55), grep -c -> 0 (61-62), glob grep -> NO_MATCHES_ANY_DOC (63-64), the 17-row census table (76-95), the disabled-row query output 'code-factory-qa|0|auto-disable|failure rate 91.3% (84/92 ticks, window 100, threshold 0.90)' (97-98), 'Rows with a non-zero ceiling: 17. Enabled among them: 16.' (100), and the prescribed one-query output (104-125). Lines 66-70 explain why the audit retains the phrase (documented glob does not descend into docs/audits/; recursive `grep -c` -> 6, all quotations). §4 gate table (155-159) records SELFTEST: PASS exit 0 at 1fea92d (base), 9149ff8 (first implementation commit) and the second implementation commit; line 161 records `bash scripts/boardctl validate` -> 'RESULT: OK (3 warning(s))'. (6) Fresh evaluator runs: `bash tests/selftest.sh` -> EXIT=0, final line 'SELFTEST: PASS'; `bash scripts/boardctl validate` -> 'RESULT: OK (3 warning(s))', EXIT=0.
